questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Actually that my girlfriend and i both were able to get spots in Melbourne. Also heard Melbourne was a cool city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was greaaaaat

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival was great. Shout out stop one they can help you with everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: To help with overlapping subjects and directions around campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were great.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very hard to find. We rented an airbnb first, then we got a room in Toorak but it was a boring naighborhood and far away. So the last 2 months we just rented an Airbnb. It helped that we were two people.

On campus housing was sooooo expensive for what you got.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
On campus housing is nice if you want to spend all your money on rent. It will be less stressful then finding of campus housing though. I think the price of a nice location Airbnb is around the same as on-campus housing but idk. It seemed like everyone had some problem with their housing.

Stay away from student accomidation called Scape! they are scams!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Wayyyy tooo expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I remember it as stressful

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Dont remember too much. But everyone wants you to succeed and help, so its okay if you fuck it up a bit

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email i guess.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got them all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get familliar with the subject handbook. Once you get it, its super helpful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It varied alot between different subjects

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Seemed like the level of the subjects were very different

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More individual. I was not on campus that often. Also seemed like they expected you to already know what you wanted to write about and explore in the subject when you showed up. they valued original though alot

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Australian surfing, Street Art, Social Policy and Urban Problems and The Economies of Cities and Regions

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Street Art: So cool! You also go on tours in Melbourne.
Social Policy and Urban Problems: Class where i learned the most. The professor knows everything about cities

If you want a complete blow-off class you can take Australian Surfing, you wont learn anything really and you will go surfing one time at a wave pool. The exam is making a Tiktok and an assignment where you can use AI

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Very expensive Visa. You should apply for the Working Visa instead of student visa as it is cheaper and it is allowed to do so. This is of course only if you do not intend on using the working visa another time

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Eating out and coffee. Also public transport was free most of the time we were there bc of fuel crisis. 

PS locals dont tap their Myki on trams. Its the culture. If you get a fine you dont even need to pay

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Surfing club was cool. People were young and mostly joined it to party

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfing. Go to tourquey and surf. Public transport there is long but it runs on time

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Surf surf surf. And dont feel too pressured to travel every weekend like alot of the danes did. I found it cooler to actually live in the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. They are more laid back and open then danes. Puts our culture to shame. Copenhageners seem so snobbish in comparison

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their Hotdogs are horrible. They use toast bread as buns???

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: its like cool to be laid back and not really give so many fucks. Makes the whole atmousphere nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go surfing in Tourquey! Registering is stressful but worth it! buy a bike i guess

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: idk

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I skateboarded alot and made australian friends that way. Its hard to make local friends at uni when you are exchange student. Also daytrips surfing at torquey and street-art excursions

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: registration and anxiety about going

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
